messages.subject: variables are global in R code chunks, but not in Python?
messages.subject_clean: variables are global in R code chunks, but not in Python?
messages.body_plain:
Hi, folks.  I'm trying to use rmarkdown/knitr in "polyglot" mode:

<https://github.com/yihui/knitr-examples/blob/master/106-polyglot.Rmd>

with various code chunks in R, Python, and bash.  It appears that variables defined in R code chunks persist across code chunks; i.e., they appear to be in a global environment.

On the contrary, variables defined in Python code chunks do *not* seem to persist across code chunks.  I'd like to know if there's some way to make the Python behavior the same as the R behavior.

Following the inverse of Yihui's good advice, I posted this issue first on stackoverflow:

<http://stackoverflow.com/questions/32958453/python-code-chunk-variable-persist-across-code-chunk>

where I have an ECM, but I seem to be the only one even looking at the post.  Suggestions welcome.

-- Mike

messages.subject: Rmarkdown Knitr table format question
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am trying to use Rmarkdown to make tables as I would like them and was hoping someone could help me. I am currently asking for a student who will be using MS Word, but I am also interested in this output for PDF.

If I run the following as a RMD script, I get tables that look like Table 1 in the picture.

---
title: "Tables with R"
fig_height: 6
fig_width: 7
output: word_document
fig_caption: yes
---

```{r, results = 'asis', echo=FALSE}
dat <- mtcars[1:5, 1:6]
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
rmarkdownTable <- function(df){
  cat(paste(names(df), collapse = "|"))
  cat("\n")
  cat(paste(rep("-", ncol(df)), collapse = "|"))
  cat("\n")

  for(i in 1:nrow(df)){
    cat(paste(df[i,], collapse = "|"))
    cat("\n")
    }
invisible(NULL)
}
```

Table 1. mtcars Data
```{r, results = 'asis', echo=FALSE}
rmarkdownTable(dat)
```

Table 1. mtcars Data
```{r, results = 'asis', echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(dat, row.names=FALSE)
```

__________________________

This is close to what I want, and is produced with the function defined above or with the knitr::kable() function.

What I really want is for the table to look like Table 2, with the additional horizontal lines:

Can someone please tell me how to modify the above function (I have tried) or what options I should use with knitr::kable() to get those additional horizontal lines.

Thank you!
Patrick

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] knitr to pdf src image issue
messages.subject_clean: [knitr] knitr to pdf src image issue
messages.body_plain: is an HTML tag, and it is not portable in the sense that Pandoc won't convert it to LaTeX. Only the Markdown syntax is portable, i.e. ![]() but you cannot set the alignment or size of the image when using the Markdown syntax. If the image is generated from an R plot, you can use chunk options fig.align, fig.with/fig.height, out.width/out.height to set the alignment/size, and knitr will automatically generate LaTeX or HTML code according to the output format. That is a portable approach. Regards, Yihui -- Yihui Xie Web: http://yihui.name On Wed, Oct 21, 2015 at 12:39 PM, Matt Giday wrote: > I have a n image that I can knit to HTML, but when knit to PDF, the image > doesn't display. Do I need to add some parameters for the pdf? > > > > > > My YAML has the following only > output: > html_document: > toc: yes > pdf_document: > toc: yes > > > Here is the version info > R version 3.2.0 (2015-04-16) > Platform:apple-darwin (64-bit) > Running under: OS X 10.10.5 (Yosemite) > > Thanks, > > Abiyu

messages.subject: Re: Clash between latex mathastext package and tikzdevice in knitr
messages.subject_clean: Clash between latex mathastext package and tikzdevice in knitr
messages.body_plain:
Hello

I answer my own question to which I've found the solution in the vignette of tikzDevice...
What is needed is to adjust the tikz options for Xelatex as in the following :

options(
tikzXelatexPackages =
c("\\usepackage{tikz}\n",
"\\usepackage[active,tightpage,xetex]{preview}\n",
"\\PassOptionsToPackage{no-math}{fontspec}\n",
"\\usepackage{fontspec,xunicode}\n",
"\\usepackage{mathastext}\n",
"\\PreviewEnvironment{pgfpicture}\n",
"\\setlength\\PreviewBorder{0pt}\n"
))

Regards,
Jacques

Le dimanche 25 octobre 2015 18:46:03 UTC+1, jro...@gmail.com a écrit :
> Hello,
>
> I'd like (1) to have my figures drawn  with tikz (through option dev='tikz'), and (2) harmonize the math font of the LaTeX document using XeLaTeX as the LaTeX compiler.
>
> However when using  \usepackage{mathastext} in order to get the same font in math as in the normal text, I get an error from tikzdevice:
>
> "Error in getMetricsFromLatex(TeXMetrics)"
>
> Commenting out the first line in the preamble solves the issue but the math font is then different from the text font:
>
> % \usepackage{mathastext}
> \PassOptionsToPackage{no-math}{fontspec}
> \usepackage{fontspec}
>
> Thanks in advance for any help,
> Jacques
